identity.title: Resolving Protoplanetary Disks at Millimeter Wavelengths with CARMA

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present continuum observations at $\lambda=1.3$ mm and 2.7 mm using the Combined Array for Research in Millimeter-wave Astronomy (CARMA) toward six protoplanetary disks in the Taurus molecular cloud

distance_source.value: adopted Taurus distance, from Bertout et al. 1999 Hipparcos ranges

evidence.quote: However, 140 pc is within uncertainties of most of the ranges, so it is adopted for all 6 targets in this study.

question.value: What are the physical properties of six Taurus protoplanetary disks from CARMA 1.3 and 2.7 mm visibilities, and does a flared power-law or flared viscous accretion disk model fit better?

evidence.quote: We constrain physical properties of the disks with Bayesian inference using two disk models; flared power-law disk model and flared accretion disk model.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00015.SV.
continuum observations at $\lambda=1.3$ mm and 2.7 mm
Individual wide bandwidth windows ($\Delta\nu \sim 500$ MHz) are averaged and considered a visibility point.

arrays.value: CARMA (6 x 10.1 m, 9 x 6.4 m; 3.5 m antennas not used for imaging)

evidence.quote: which is a heterogeneous array consisting of six 10.1-m, nine 6.4-m, and eight 3.5-m antennas. For this project the 3.5-m antennas were not used for imaging.

configurations.value: A, B, C and/or D configurations

evidence.quote: All targets were observed in A and/or B configurations (see Table [\[tab_diskobs\]](#tab_diskobs)) at $\lambda=1.3$ mm and/or 3 mm
The highest angular resolution (the smallest synthesized beam size) is $\sim$0.13$''$ at $\lambda=1.3$ mm toward HL Tau.

max_recoverable_scale.value: at least 10 arcsec (min uv distance at most 17 kλ)

evidence.quote: the minimum *uv* distance is at most 17 kilo-wavelengths, which means that our large scale sensitivity is at least 10 arcseconds.

observing_dates.value: 2007 Sep to 2011 Jan (per track in Table 2)

provided.value: HL Tau long-baseline Science Verification data, used only qualitatively for comparison

evidence.quote: the long baseline science verification (SV) data of ALMA have recently shown unprecedented details of substructures toward HL Tau

evidence.quote: Selected information from the above studies is summarized in Table [\[tab_targets\]](#tab_targets).

MIRIAD (cite: sault1995) has been employed to calibrate and map data. Individual tracks have been calibrated and verified separately then combined

evidence.quote: In fact, this paper uses the same data set of HL Tau but we employ two disk models and a better temperature distribution.

evidence.quote: which are generally a few times larger than the theoretical estimate (cite: 2011ApJ...741....3K)

method.value: MIRIAD calibration per track with test-calibrator checks and CPACS for some tracks; combine tracks in invert step; robust 0

evidence.quote: MIRIAD (cite: sault1995) has been employed to calibrate and map data.
the weighting scheme with a robust value of 0 has been applied.

validation.value: test calibrator point-likeness and flat gain-calibrator uv amplitudes

evidence.quote: All of our data sets have a flat amplitude slope of gain calibrators after calibration

method.value: RADMC 3D Monte Carlo radiative transfer, fit with weighted midplane and surface functional forms

evidence.quote: we make a functional form weighting two functions that fit to the mid-plane ($T_m$) and surface temperature distributions ($T_s$)

assumptions.value: kappa0 = 0.01 cm2/g at 230 GHz, gas-to-dust 100, dust and gas temperature equal, scale height not updated from temperature

evidence.quote: In addition, we assume a gas-to-dust mass ratio of 100.

analysis_steps.goal: model visibilities for each disk model and vertical structure

method.value: build 2D disk models with radiative transfer along line of sight, multiply by three CARMA primary beams, Fourier transform and sample at observed uv points

evidence.quote: Then, the actual model visibilities are sampled in the *uv* coverage of observational data by bi-linear interpolation of the model visibility maps.

we carry out 25 separate models for each target: $b_t = \{0.6, 0.8,
1.0, 1.2, 1.4\}$ and $h = \{0.95, 1.10, 1.25, 1.40, 1.55\}$
an image pixel size of 9 AU and an image size of 1024 pixel by 1024 pixel are used

assumptions.value: distance 140 pc; constant beta; accretion disk cut at 5 Rc

evidence.quote: the modeling disks are cut off at 5 $R_c$ due to limitation in image size and for simplicity in integration

method.value: Metropolis-Hastings MCMC with Gaussian likelihood on real and imaginary visibilities; 8 random starts, annealing, then fresh run per (b_t,h) with proposal tuned to 10-50% acceptance

evidence.quote: Searching distributions of model parameters by the Metropolis Hastings method has two parts.

key_parameters.value: 7 free parameters: s, beta, Mdisk, Rin, Rout (or Rc), inclination, PA

evidence.quote: There are 7 free parameters for each disk model: $s$, $\beta$, $M_{disk}$, $R_{in}$, $R_{out}$ (or $R_c$), $\theta_i$, and $PA$.

fitting.value: Metropolis-Hastings; Gaussian likelihood; uniform priors over same ranges for both models; no priors from images except centers and inclination sign

evidence.quote: We set the prior as well as the number of free parameters the same for the two models (uniform priors over the same ranges)

validation.value: residual maps and annular-averaged visibility plots

evidence.quote: The low levels of the residual indicate excellence of our model fitting.

method.value: Bayes factor K from best likelihood times posterior volume; K>3 favors accretion disk

evidence.quote: The likelihood integration can be estimated by the best likelihood times the posterior accessible volume
$K > 3$ indicates a considerable preference for the model of the numerator

method.value: Pearson correlation among fitted properties; Toomre Q profile from midplane temperature and surface density; alpha from accretion rate

evidence.quote: We calculated correlations between the constrained physical properties
regions of $Q \lesssim 1.5$ are gravitationally unstable

assumptions.value: Keplerian rotation; Haro 6-13 accretion rate assumed 1.0e-7 Msun/yr

evidence.quote:
We assumed the accretion rate of Haro 6-13, which has not been reported, as a typical value of $1.0\times 10^{-7}~\textrm{M}_\ensuremath{\odot}~
\textrm{year}^{-1}$.
MIRIAD (cite: sault1995) has been employed to calibrate and map data.
we use a temperature distribution calculated in a given disk structure by the RADMC 3D code

used_for.value: Gaussian random numbers for MCMC proposals

evidence.quote: The GASDEV subroutine of the Numerical Recipes using the Box-Muller method is used to produce random numbers in the Gaussian distribution

results_numeric.quantity: ln K HL Tau (accretion vs power-law)

evidence.quote: $\beta$ of our sample disks ranges from -0.15 to 0.70 and half of them are around 0
Disk masses are 0.01–0.10 M$_\odot$.

findings_qualitative.value: Extended disks (CI Tau, DL Tau, HL Tau) prefer thinner, less flared models; DO Tau prefers thick, flared

evidence.quote: the three extended disks (CI Tau, DL Tau, and HL Tau) have higher posteriors in thinner and less flared models.

findings_qualitative.value: Weak non-axisymmetric feature in CI Tau at both wavelengths; no Q<1.5 region found

evidence.quote: the well-resolved map of CI Tau has a weak substructure that is seen at both wavelengths

claims.hypothesis: Does the accretion disk model fit better than the power-law model?
claims.experiment: Bayes factors from visibility fits of six disks
claims.result: ln K positive for all but DL Tau; large for HL Tau
claims.finding: accretion disk model preferred overall, with DL Tau exception

evidence.quote: Therefore, we conclude that overall the accretion disk model is preferred.

claims.hypothesis: Do beta, mass and density gradient correlate, indicating grain growth and drift?
claims.experiment: correlation coefficients among fitted properties of six disks
claims.result: beta correlates with mass (0.84), anticorrelates with s (-0.77)
claims.finding: large grains in less massive disks with steeper midplane gradients

evidence.quote: We found a correlation between $\beta$ and the disk masses: disks with a smaller $\beta$ are less massive.

claims.hypothesis: Do extended disks show gravitational instability?
claims.result: CI Tau and DL Tau have no Q<1.5 region; DL Tau near 1.5 at ~100 AU

evidence.quote: CI Tau and DL Tau have the smallest $Q$ minima with HL Tau, but they do not have a region with $Q<1.5$.

why_this_method.value: Bayesian inference provides parameter distributions and model comparison unlike chi-square

evidence.quote: The Bayesian approach provides a basis of probability theory to compare two models as well as to achieve parameter probability distributions, which are not given by the $\chi^2$ method.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Center positions from manual intensity peaks tested; Gaussian-fit offsets chosen for higher posteriors

evidence.quote: The offset values by the simple Gaussian fit have been chosen (Table [\[tab_diskdata\]](#tab_diskdata)), as they give higher posteriors.

limitations_admitted.value: Inner radii unreliable due to resolution and decoherence; constant beta assumed; kappa0 uncertain by factor two

evidence.quote: fitted values can be model-dependent and are likely unreliable due to systematic uncertainties in the observation, primarily the resolution.

referee_caveats_inferred: Bayes factor approximated by best likelihood times posterior width rather than true evidence integral
Only six targets, so correlations are weak statistically
Results dependent on assumed kappa0 and constant beta
Disagrees with Guilloteau et al. on model preference and beta radial variation

data_public_as_stated.value: HL Tau ALMA SV data cited; CARMA data not stated as public

evidence.quote: This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00015.SV.
